nodes.label: TypeSafe / Diogo Almeida
nodes.summary: TypeSafe company-news post announcing Jev, its first public System One Model, in early access. System One models are a class of frontier models built to make fast, structured decisions that software can use directly, trained with Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions (RLCD). The page calls Jev a frontier-intelligence function call: unstructured state in, typed probabilistic decisions out. It gives up string generation, is optimized for structured outputs, and can't hallucinate. The class name draws on Kahneman's fast System 1 thinking; Jev is named after William Stanley Jevons.
nodes.notes: Company News by Diogo Almeida, founder of TypeSafe, dated Sep 15, 2026. This Jev is TypeSafe's decision model, not a Vercel product.

nodes.notes: ~2.1k stars, MIT, Node 22+. Needs a key for Vercel AI Gateway, TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or OpenCode Zen. nodes.label: Andrej Karpathy (LLM Wiki)
nodes.summary: Idea file for a personal knowledge base: an LLM incrementally maintains a persistent, interlinked markdown wiki (summaries, entity and concept pages, index.md, and an append-only log.md) between the user and immutable raw sources, instead of re-deriving answers from retrieved chunks on every query. Operations named in the file: ingest, query (file useful answers back into the wiki), and lint. The file says it is abstract and not a specific implementation.
nodes.notes: Public GitHub gist by karpathy (id 442a6bf555914893e9891c11519de94f), not a repository. Three layers named in the file: raw sources, the wiki, and a schema (examples given: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md). Optional local search tool cited: qmd, which the gist says has a CLI and an MCP server. Related idea cited: Vannevar Bush's Memex (1945). The file says an index can work at moderate scale (about 100 sources and hundreds of pages) without embedding-based RAG.

nodes.label: Zep (Graphiti)
nodes.summary: Graphiti is a framework for building and querying temporally-aware knowledge graphs, specifically tailored for AI agents operating in dynamic environments.
nodes.notes: 31394 GitHub stars. License Apache-2.0. Language Python. Install with pip install graphiti-core. README also includes an MCP server. Zep temporal knowledge graph for agents, not a RAG guide.

nodes.label: mcpc / apify
nodes.summary: A universal CLI client for MCP. mcpc supports persistent sessions, stdio/HTTP, OAuth 2.1, tasks, JSON output for code mode, proxy for AI sandboxes, x402, and more.
nodes.notes: כלי CLI אוניברסלי ל-MCP. תומך בסשנים מתמשכים, משימות, פלט JSON למצב קוד וסנדבוקס ל-AI.

nodes.label: skybridge / alpic-ai
nodes.summary: Full-stack TypeScript and React framework for MCP Apps and ChatGPT apps. Type-safe tools-to-views, a local emulator with HMR, and one app that runs in Claude, ChatGPT, and other MCP UI clients.
nodes.notes: ~2.1k stars, MIT. Start with npm create skybridge@latest, or npx skills add alpic-ai/skybridge -s skybridge. Docs at https://docs.skybridge.tech. Deploy on Alpic or any Node host.

nodes.label: Serena / oraios
nodes.summary: Serena is an MCP toolkit that gives coding agents IDE-like semantic code retrieval, editing, refactoring, and debugging tools at the symbol level. It runs as an MCP server that clients such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and JetBrains assistants can launch or connect to over HTTP.
nodes.notes: 29,955 stars. License: GPL-3.0-or-later for the Serena application and MIT for SolidLSP (src/solidlsp); GitHub reports the repo license as Other. Language: Python. Install with uv (`uv tool install -p 3.13 serena-agent`), then connect the client to the Serena MCP server.

nodes.label: morluto / rea

nodes.notes: ~20.6k★, MIT, TypeScript; npx rea-agents setup; supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI
